dossiers.title: Destiny 2: The Final Shape
dossiers.summary: Destiny 2 expansion built around the Prismatic subclass, a campaign in the Pale Heart, and new supers; the accessible Steam review index was too sparse to support recurring user-review themes in this run.

observations.statement: The expansion's defining system is Prismatic, which combines abilities from multiple Light and Darkness subclasses into custom builds.
The store description frames the package around a campaign, a new destination, and new supers rather than a standalone game.

dossiers.title: Resident Evil Deluxe Origins Bundle / Biohazard Deluxe Origins Bundle
dossiers.summary: Steam app 304240 is the Resident Evil HD remaster: deliberate survival horror built around mansion exploration, puzzles, scarce resources and inventory management. Reviews praise its atmosphere and remake quality, while some players find the inventory limits, backtracking and door transitions dated or tedious.

observations.statement: Multiple reviews praise the mansion's survival-horror design and the remake's preservation of the original game's atmosphere.
Several reviews describe limited inventory, repeated backtracking and room-transition door animations as dated friction.
Resource scarcity and constrained inventory are repeatedly described as central to the game's tension and planning.

conflicts.statement: The same old-school constraints are praised as core survival-horror design by some reviewers and criticized as tedious by others.

dossiers.title: Hentai Girl Karen
dossiers.summary: A very simple tile-swapping picture puzzle with no time or score pressure. The small accessible review sample characterizes it as deliberately shallow, repetitive and suited to brief, low-effort play rather than deep puzzle design.

observations.statement: The core interaction is a basic tile-swapping picture puzzle with no time or star limit.
One detailed accessible review describes the gameplay as repetitive and lacking depth, while still functioning as a casual time-killer.

dossiers.title: Prototype™
dossiers.summary: Open-world action game focused on aggressive shape-shifting combat and unusually free traversal across the city. Reviews continue to praise movement and power fantasy, but the PC version has recurring technical compatibility and stability complaints, often accompanied by community-fix recommendations.

observations.statement: Recent reviews repeatedly praise the freedom of movement, traversal and shape-shifting combat as the game's strongest enduring qualities.
Multiple Steam reviews report PC-port stability or compatibility problems and point to community fixes or mods.

conflicts.statement: The core action is still widely enjoyed, but technical PC issues can materially affect the out-of-box experience.

dossiers.title: DEEEER Simulator: Your Average Everyday Deer Game
dossiers.summary: A short-form physics sandbox whose appeal is absurd destruction, animal gags and emergent chaos rather than deep systems. The accessible reviews strongly reinforce the comedy and destructive freedom; isolated feedback mentions unruly controls.

observations.statement: Reviews repeatedly frame the game's main appeal as chaotic physics, destruction and absurd animal interactions.
One accessible review found the controls difficult to get comfortable with.

dossiers.title: Shadow Warrior 3: Definitive Edition
dossiers.summary: Fast, arena-oriented FPS mixing gunplay, melee combat and movement. Reviews frequently enjoy the combat's speed and spectacle, but a recurring criticism is that the campaign is very short; some also describe arena encounters and enemy use as repetitive.

observations.statement: Accessible reviews describe the combat as fast, energetic and fun, consistent with the store's emphasis on gunplay, melee and movement.
Several highly rated reviews criticize the campaign for being unusually short.
More than one review describes arena fights or enemy encounters as becoming predictable or repetitive.

conflicts.statement: The combat is often praised even by reviewers who criticize the game's length and repetition.

dossiers.title: Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth: Complete Edition
dossiers.summary: Large two-game creature-collecting JRPG package with turn-based combat and extensive evolution/team-building systems. Reviews repeatedly praise the roster depth and long-form progression, while also citing grind, reused content, unclear progression and uneven localization as recurring drawbacks.

observations.statement: Reviews repeatedly praise the large Digimon roster and flexible evolution/team-building systems as a major source of long-term engagement.
Several reviews describe completionist play, evolution requirements and side content as grind-heavy or repetitive.
Multiple reviews call out weak or confusing localization, especially in Cyber Sleuth dialogue and side content.
Some reviews note reused maps or unclear next-step guidance during progression.

conflicts.statement: The same volume of collection and progression content is a strength for dedicated players and a source of grind fatigue for completionists.

dossiers.title: The Coma 2: Vicious Sisters
dossiers.summary: Story-driven 2D Korean survival horror combining exploration, puzzles, resource use and evasion. Accessible reviews often view it as an improvement over the first game and praise pacing, art and atmosphere, though a minority criticize repetitive dialogue, backtracking and underused survival items.

observations.statement: Multiple accessible reviews praise the sequel's pacing and overall improvement over the first game.
The game centers on exploration, puzzle-solving, scavenging and evasion across the Sehwa district.
One substantial negative review criticizes repeated backtracking and dialogue and argues that some survival items feel unnecessary.

conflicts.statement: Most sampled reviews describe a stronger sequel, while an opposing review sees little improvement and more repetition.

dossiers.title: Paper Dolls: Original / 纸人
dossiers.summary: First-person Chinese horror adventure built around mansion exploration, puzzles, stealth and a distinctly Eastern supernatural atmosphere. Reviews praise presentation and puzzle ideas, while recurring complaints include control/input friction and localization barriers in some puzzles.

observations.statement: Reviews praise the game's Eastern-horror atmosphere and puzzle-driven exploration as distinctive strengths.
More than one review reports control or input frustration, including keys not responding reliably.
More than one review notes language or localization barriers that can make some puzzle information harder to use.

dossiers.title: A Monster's Expedition
dossiers.summary: Polished open-world puzzle game that builds a large interconnected archipelago from simple log-pushing rules. Reviews strongly praise its puzzle craft, nonlinear exploration and cozy presentation, while also agreeing that optional content can become genuinely difficult and that repetition may wear on some players.

observations.statement: Many reviews praise the way simple log-pushing rules develop into clever, interconnected puzzle mechanics.
Reviews repeatedly value the open map because players can leave a difficult route and explore elsewhere.
Several reviews stress that the calm presentation hides substantial puzzle difficulty, especially in optional or completionist content.
A minority of reviews find the repeated tree-pushing loop monotonous despite acknowledging the game's polish.

conflicts.statement: The core log-pushing loop is celebrated for depth by many reviewers but experienced as repetitive by a smaller group.
